title: Band-9 Samples: Do you think you will watch more TV or fewer TV programmes/shows in the future? [Why/why not?]
content:
This post contains ideas and band-9 sample answers (audio included) for the Cambridge IELTS 13 Academic Speaking Part 1 Question 4 Test 1 question:

“Do you think you will watch more TV or fewer TV programmes/shows in the future? [Why/why not?]”

Sample 1: Less

In the foreseeable future, I anticipate watching less traditional television. The primary reason for this is the advent of digital platforms like Netflix and Amazon Prime, which are gradually replacing conventional TV. These platforms provide a wealth of choices, making it easier to find content tailored to my specific tastes. Additionally, they offer the convenience of viewing at any time, eliminating the need to plan my schedule around broadcast times.

Sample 2: Less

Personally, I envisage a reduction in my TV-watching habits. The rationale behind my assertion is my increasing focus on personal development activities such as reading, exercise, and learning new skills. Although television can offer educational content, I find the interactive and engaging nature of other activities more beneficial for my intellectual and physical growth.

Sample 3: Less

I predict my consumption of television programs will dwindle in the future. My growing fondness for outdoor activities like hiking, camping, and photography is primarily responsible for this shift. By spending time in nature, I not only boost my physical health but also enjoy a sense of tranquility that TV cannot provide.

Sample 4: Less

In the future, I expect my television viewing hours to diminish significantly, primarily due to escalating career commitments. As I ascend in my professional journey, the demands of my job are likely to increase, leaving me with less leisure time. Additionally, I’ve been exploring opportunities for side hustles to augment my income. These entrepreneurial ventures, although rewarding, are time-intensive. Consequently, my spare moments are more likely to be invested in productive pursuits rather than passive television viewing.

Sample 5: More

Interestingly enough, my profession might actually necessitate me to watch more television in the coming years. As a media analyst, staying abreast of the latest trends in television programming is crucial. If I fail to do so, it might impair my capacity to deliver insightful analysis for my clients. Hence, watching more television becomes a practical solution to meet my professional demands.

Sample 6: More

My consumption of television broadcasts will increase in the future. At the end of a hard day, there’s nothing I enjoy more than curling up on the sofa with a cup of tea and immersing myself in the world of my favorite characters. As life gets busier, these moments of escapism become even more precious, making me inclined towards watching more television.

Sample 7: More

I predict my television viewing will rise in the future, primarily due to its role in fostering social connections. In this globalized world, popular television series often become the epicenter of discussions among friends, families, and even on social platforms. Participating in these discussions not only enhances my social interactions but also keeps me updated with global events and trends.

Sample 8: More

I reckon I’ll be spending more time on TV in the forthcoming years, primarily due to the leaps and bounds made in terms of accessibility. With the advent of smart televisions, mobile apps, and online streaming platforms, we can now watch our favorite shows whenever we want, wherever we are. This flexibility, coupled with an increasing variety of high-quality content, makes it highly likely that I will be watching more TV.

Sample 9: Not Sure

Predicting my future television consumption is rather challenging. As my professional commitments intensify, I may have less time to devote to watching TV shows. However, I might adopt a more selective approach, focusing only on quality content that truly captures my interest, thereby balancing my time effectively.

Sample 10: Not Sure

Frankly, it’s a bit of a conundrum predicting my future television viewing habits. They could swing either way, largely influenced by my social dynamics. If my future circle of friends and family are avid television enthusiasts, I might find myself watching more TV to partake in the shared experience. Conversely, if I find myself amidst people who prefer other activities like sports, reading, or travel, my television consumption might diminish.
